harmonicFunction: Am7 (i7) - Heavy, blues-drenched minor tonic anchor with Leslie swirl
Dm7 (iv7) - Minor subdominant deepening the melancholy blues narrative
F9 (♭VI9) - Soulful substitute chord building tension before the turnaround
E7#9 (V7#9) - The iconic Jimi Hendrix/Texas altered dominant injecting maximum tension before the tonic resolution

techniques.name: Texas Shuffle Muted String Rakes & Vibratone Rotary Swirl
techniques.description: Raking across multiple muted strings to land on punchy double-stops and triad chords while maintaining a driving shuffle rhythm

notes: Bass shuffle: Open low E to 5th fret A root, followed by 7th-fret D/G string chord stabs
Turnaround: F9 shape (X-8-7-8-8-X) sliding down to E7#9 (X-7-6-7-8-X)
Albert King bends: 8th fret high E string bent full step with heavy finger vibrato
sequence: Mute non-played strings with left-hand index finger
Rake downward across muted strings to hit the target chords with percussive attack
Maintain a deep shuffle pulse (triplet feel) with your right hand
Slide smoothly between F9 and E7#9 on beat 1 and 2 of the turnaround
tips: SRV used heavy guitar strings (.013–.058 gauge) tuned down a half-step for colossal tone
The rotary swirl came from a vintage Fender Vibratone cabinet (Leslie rotating foam drum)
Dig in hard with the pick edge—SRV played with incredible physical intensity

techniques.name: Albert King Upside-Down Bending & Minor Blues Turnaround Shifts
techniques.description: Albert King-inspired string bending targeting minor and major 3rd blue notes combined with altered dominant chord substitutions

notes: Bend 8th fret on high E (C) full step to D with 3-finger reinforcement
Target note F# (natural 6th in Dorian): 7th fret B string or 4th fret D string
Slide from F9 (X-8-7-8-8-X) to E7#9 (X-7-6-7-8-X) on beats 1 and 2 of bar 9
sequence: Fret high E at fret 8 and push upward toward the ceiling with index, middle, and ring fingers
Apply wide, circular wrist vibrato at the crest of the bend
Release cleanly down to fret 5 without unwanted open-string noise
Hit the altered E7#9 chord hard with a downward pick sweep
tips: Keep the underside of your fretting hand fingers muting the adjacent G and B strings
Use a stiff, heavy pick for zero deflection during aggressive downstroke rakes
Blend the neck and middle pickups on your Stratocaster to capture SRV's woody woman tone

sections.name: Leslie Shuffle Riff (Verse Vamp)
sections.technique: Texas Shuffle Muted String Rakes & Vibratone Rotary Swirl
sections.description: Stevie's hypnotic opening rhythm combining low bass shuffle notes with swirling chorused chord stabs.
notes: Tune down half a step (Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb)
Lock in with the triplet shuffle feel
Rake across muted strings before hitting the chord

sections.name: Turnaround Chords (F9 to E7#9)
sections.technique: Albert King Upside-Down Bending & Minor Blues Turnaround Shifts
sections.description: The dramatic 9th-chord turnaround sliding from F9 into the biting E7#9.
notes: Crisp downward slide from fret 8 to 7
Accentuate the high G note on the E7#9 shape
Resolve cleanly back into the low A root

sections.name: Verse 1 Vocal Shuffle & Muted Rakes
sections.technique: Texas Shuffle Muted String Rakes & Vibratone Rotary Swirl
sections.description: Subtle dynamic comping backing the vocals with percussive string damping.
notes: Keep the rhythm loose and conversational
Mute strings sharply with the fretting hand on offbeats
Prepare for the upcoming solo explosion

sections.name: Main Blues Solo (Chorus 1 - Albert King Bends)
sections.technique: Albert King Upside-Down Bending & Minor Blues Turnaround Shifts
sections.description: Stevie's signature slow-blues lead phrasing featuring aggressive string bends and wide vibrato.
notes: Support full bends with three fretting fingers
Apply wide, rhythmic wrist vibrato
Dig into the pick attack for natural tube breakup

sections.name: Main Blues Solo (Chorus 2 - Rotary Swirl & Double Stops)
sections.technique: Albert King Upside-Down Bending & Minor Blues Turnaround Shifts
sections.description: High-energy second solo chorus with rotary Leslie speaker swirl and stinging 5th-position double stops.
sections.progression: Am7 - Dm7 - Am7 - F9 - E7#9 - Am7
notes: Engage Tube Screamer to boost the rotating speaker sound
Strike 5th-fret double stops across strings 1 and 2 with an aggressive downward rake
Curl the minor third slightly sharp before resolving to root A

sections.name: Outro Shuffle Groove & Decrescendo
sections.technique: Texas Shuffle Muted String Rakes & Vibratone Rotary Swirl
sections.description: Hypnotic repetition of the main Leslie shuffle riff decaying into the room fade.
notes: Return to the steady, unhurried bass-and-rake engine
Gradual volume decay as the rhythm section locks into the final groove
Final raked Am7 chord sustaining with Leslie swirl

amp.recommended: Fender Super Reverb & Fender Vibroverb with Fender Vibratone Leslie cab

effects.distortion: Ibanez TS9 / TS808 Tube Screamer (gain low, level high as clean boost)
effects.chorus: Fender Vibratone rotating Leslie speaker (or Neo Instruments Ventilator pedal)

beginner.title: Minor Blues Chords
steps: Learn the basic 12-bar minor blues progression: Am7, Dm7, and E7
Practice counting the triplet shuffle groove (1-trip-let, 2-trip-let)
Strum in quarter notes at 80 BPM

intermediate.title: The Shuffle Rake & Turnaround
steps: Master the percussive string rake into the Am7 chord stabs
Learn the F9 and E7#9 turnaround shapes and transitions
Play along with the studio track at 105 BPM

advanced.title: Texas Lead & Albert King Bends
steps: Nail the solo note-for-note with authentic Stevie Ray Vaughan bending and vibrato
Incorporate dynamic muted rakes into every lead lick
Capture the authentic Leslie speaker rotary feel and aggressive touch

commonMistakes: Playing straight eighth notes instead of the deep swing triplet shuffle
Letting adjacent strings buzz during muted string rakes
Under-bending on the 8th fret B and E strings
practiceRoutine: 5 minutes: Shuffle rake technique isolated on Am7 at 90 BPM
5 minutes: Turnaround chord transitions (F9 → E7#9 → Am7)
5 minutes: String bending intonation drill with tuner
5 minutes: Full solo playthrough with backing track
metronomeWork: Set metronome to triplet shuffle feel at 85 BPM, gradually advancing to 105 BPM
Ensure downbeat bass notes land firmly on the beat
